Houston, We Have an Ongoing FAA Problem

The safety of America’s air-transportation system is too important for unanswered questions.

Regarding your editorial “ Just Another Frantic Friday at the FAA ” (Nov. 16): The nationwide air traffic shutdown on Nov. 13 raises questions that deserve answers. The Trump administration eliminated hundreds of Federal Aviation Administration positions in 2025, including some involved in maintaining aviation equipment. Congress has already appropriated billions to modernize the nation’s aging air-traffic control system. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is now asking Congress for another $50 billion.

Before appropriating more money, Congress should determine how previously authorized funds have been used and whether staffing reductions contributed to the failure. The Government Accountability Office warned in September that the FAA’s modernization program lacked an integrated schedule and reliable overall cost estimates.
